newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Bearish trend persists on Nigerian stock market.
newsitem.headline: Bearish trend persists on Nigerian stock market.

text.p: The long bearish trend persisted on the Nigerian stock market on Wednesday as chemical companies joined the big four banks, leading manufacturers and petroleum producers on the debit side, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 8621.43 from 8642.23 on Tuesday.

Chemical and Allied Products, a leading paint manufacturer, on Wednesday reported a loss of 206.651 million naira for fiscal 1996 from a profit of 62.979 million naira a year earlier. It closed 10 kobo lower at 4.20 naira. Berger Paints also ended 10 kobo down at 4.10 naira.
First Bank ended at 13.90 naira, the same as Union Bank, while Afribank was 7.90 naira, all 10 kobo lower. UBA closed at 12.15 naira, five kobo down.
Nigerian Breweries was down 18 kobo to 20 naira and West African Portland Cement Co dropped two kobo to 65.23 naira.
Ashaka Cement was the worse hit, sliding 20 kobo to 13.50 naira. The trend did not spare Lever Brothers, which shed 10 kobo to 28.50 naira and PZ Industries, which fell 30 kobo to 29.35 naira.
Nigeria's oldest trading company, UAC tumbled 25 kobo to 17.05 naira, while leading insurance firm, AIICO was 20 kobo weaker at 15.30 naira.
Nigerian Tobacco fell by the maximum five percent, or 14 kobo, to 2.76 naira because of a recent poor result.
Agip oil company continued its free fall. It lost 25 kobo again at 22.00 naira. African Petroleum too shed 20 kobo at 57.65 naira.
But Mobil and Texaco continued to find buyers and ended stronger. Mobil gained 10 kobo to finish at 64.10 naira and Texaco rose five kobo to 49.40 naira.
Food firm Nestle soared to 43.25 naira, up 25 kobo, fuelled by growing demand, dealers said.

Also, Guaranty Trust Bank led relatively small banks in ascending. It ended 10 kobo higher at 13.20 naira. FSB International Bank ended at 4.15 naira, five kobo more and Wema Bank added six kobo to 2.81 naira.
